# Reasons

Every refusal carries a reason: a stable code and the values involved (14 §5). A verb that declines, a command refused, a fault while a rule runs are reported with one. Mods add their own with the [`reason`](types/reason.md) type and give them with `cancel_event`.

- <a id="ability-bad-argument"></a>`ability.bad_argument`: A verb of abilities was given an argument that is missing or of the wrong kind. Values: `arg`, the argument's name.
- <a id="ability-bad-rank"></a>`ability.bad_rank`: A rank is not a whole number from 0 to 10,000. Values: `rank`.
- <a id="ability-condition"></a>`ability.condition`: The grant's `if` does not hold. Values: `ability`, `action`.
- <a id="ability-cooling-down"></a>`ability.cooling_down`: The grant is waiting out its cooldown. Values: `ability`, `action`, `left`: seconds of the owner's own time.
- <a id="ability-cost-short"></a>`ability.cost_short`: A cost is more than its pool holds, with whatever overdraw allows (08 §5.2). Values: `entity` (who pays), `pool`, `wanted`, `have`, `short`: what is missing.
- <a id="ability-cost-source-gone"></a>`ability.cost_source_gone`: A cost drawn `from` something gives no entity that exists and has the pool. Values: `ability`, `pool`.
- <a id="ability-cost-unknown"></a>`ability.cost_unknown`: A cost names a pool or an item that is not loaded. Values: `cost`.
- <a id="ability-dormant"></a>`ability.dormant`: The ability is dormant: its `while` does not hold (08 §6.1). Values: `ability`.
- <a id="ability-items-short"></a>`ability.items_short`: Fewer items of a kind are held than a cost consumes. Values: `item`, `wanted`, `have`.
- <a id="ability-mode-off"></a>`ability.mode_off`: The mode is not on. Values: `ability`, `mode`.
- <a id="ability-mode-on"></a>`ability.mode_on`: The mode is on already. Values: `ability`, `mode`.
- <a id="ability-mode-unknown"></a>`ability.mode_unknown`: The ability has no mode of that id. Values: `ability`, `mode`.
- <a id="ability-no-grant"></a>`ability.no_grant`: The ability grants no such action, or grants several and none was named. Values: `ability`, `action` (empty when none was named).
- <a id="ability-not-held"></a>`ability.not_held`: The entity does not hold the ability, or it was revoked. Values: `entity`, `ability`.
- <a id="ability-not-registered"></a>`ability.not_registered`: The definitions were loaded without the `ability` definition type. Values: none.
- <a id="ability-rank-from-track"></a>`ability.rank_from_track`: `set_rank` was asked of an ability whose rank is its track's level: advance the track. Values: `ability`.
- <a id="ability-rank-too-low"></a>`ability.rank_too_low`: The ability's rank is below the `at_rank` of the grant or mode. Values: `ability`, `rank`, `needed`.
- <a id="ability-unknown"></a>`ability.unknown`: The id is not an `ability` definition. Values: `ability`, as given.
- <a id="ability-upkeep"></a>`ability.upkeep`: A mode's upkeep cannot be met: the entity lacks the pool or it is empty. Values: `ability`, `mode`, `pool`.
- <a id="action-bad-time"></a>`action.bad_time`: An action's tempo came out at zero or below, or null; a phase's `time` or `max` below zero or null; or a tick's `every` at zero or below, or null. A fault: the tempo counts as 1, the duration as none, and the tick does not repeat. Values: `action`, `phase`.
- <a id="action-interrupted"></a>`action.interrupted`: The `interrupt` effect ended the action. The reason `action_interrupted` carries. Values: `action`.
- <a id="action-not-running"></a>`action.not_running`: `Cancel` named an action that is not running, or is not the entity's. Values: `entity`, `action`.
- <a id="action-unknown"></a>`action.unknown`: No action definition has the id that was given. Values: `action`.
- <a id="advance-tick-limit"></a>`advance.tick_limit`: More wake-ups ran at one tick than the limit allows; the advance yielded. Values: `tick`, `limit`.
- <a id="advance-unhandled-wake"></a>`advance.unhandled_wake`: A wake-up was due and nothing handles its domain. It was dropped. Values: `domain`, `id`, `arg`.
- <a id="ai-bad-value"></a>`ai.bad_value`: A verb of minds was given an argument it cannot use. Values: `argument`.
- <a id="ai-cancelled"></a>`ai.cancelled`: A step's action was cancelled by something other than the mind that started it. Values: `action`.
- <a id="ai-goal-failed"></a>`ai.goal_failed`: A goal's `fail` held. Values: `goal`.
- <a id="ai-no-go-action"></a>`ai.no_go_action`: A step that moves, for a mind that names no `go_action`. Values: `entity`.
- <a id="ai-no-method"></a>`ai.no_method`: No method of a goal could be used: none's `if` held, or each failed in this pursuit. The goal fails. Values: `goal`.
- <a id="ai-no-mind-def"></a>`ai.no_mind_def`: The character thinks by no `mind` definition: it has no mind, or its mind's profile names none. Values: `entity`.
- <a id="ai-no-option"></a>`ai.no_option`: A `choose` step found no action tagged with its purpose that could start. Values: `purpose`.
- <a id="ai-no-target"></a>`ai.no_target`: A step's target named no place the mind knows of: null, or someone it has no track of. Values: `step`.
- <a id="ai-no-way-out"></a>`ai.no_way_out`: A `keep_from` step found no place it believes it can reach that is further from what it keeps from. Values: `entity`.
- <a id="ai-not-arrived"></a>`ai.not_arrived`: A step that moves ended short of where it was going: its action ended there, or no way was found. Values: `entity`.
- <a id="ai-refused"></a>`ai.refused`: A handler of `action_starting` refused a step's action. Values: `action`.
- <a id="ai-unknown-goal"></a>`ai.unknown_goal`: `set_goal` named no goal that is loaded. Values: `argument`.
- <a id="bad-selection"></a>`bad_selection`: A selection does not suit its choice: an option it does not have, too many or too few, over budget, out of range, too long, or of the wrong shape. Values: `choice`, `why`.
- <a id="clock-bad-rate"></a>`clock.bad_rate`: A clock's rate must be zero or more, and finite.
- <a id="clock-loop"></a>`clock.loop`: The clock would be placed under itself or one of its descendants.
- <a id="clock-unknown"></a>`clock.unknown`: No clock has this id: it was never created, or it has been destroyed.
- <a id="combat-bad-number"></a>`combat.bad_number`: A number a strike needs came out as nothing it can use: an energy or a reach below zero or not finite, a push or an effort outside 0 to 1, a lift that is not finite. Values: `what`, `value`.
- <a id="combat-defended"></a>`combat.defended`: A strike reached its target and nothing of it was delivered: the defences in force turned it aside, and what was put in the way took the rest (07 §5.3). Carried by `strike_stopped`. Values: `target`.
- <a id="combat-no-attack"></a>`combat.no_attack`: A `strike` is written in a list that belongs to no action, or names an attack its action does not have, or names none in an action that has several. Values: `action`, `attack`.
- <a id="combat-no-surface"></a>`combat.no_surface`: The attacker has nothing that answers to the attack's `with`: no working part of that name with that surface, no item held with that tag and surface. Values: `action`, `attack`, `with`.
- <a id="combat-no-target"></a>`combat.no_target`: A `strike` was given neither an entity to strike nor a cell, or a target that is not in the world. Values: `target`.
- <a id="combat-not-its-part"></a>`combat.not_its_part`: The part a strike is aimed at is not a part of the entity it strikes. Values: `target`.
- <a id="combat-nothing-gripped"></a>`combat.nothing_gripped`: The attack strikes with something gripped (07 §9), and the attacker grips nothing: grips are not built yet. Values: `action`, `attack`.
- <a id="combat-nothing-there"></a>`combat.nothing_there`: A strike at a cell found the cell not loaded, outside its grid, or holding no floor, block or fixture. Values: `cell`.
- <a id="combat-too-deep"></a>`combat.too_deep`: A strike was resolved inside eight others: one whose `on_land` started an action that struck at once, and so on. Values: `limit`.
- <a id="command-bad-argument"></a>`command.bad_argument`: A command carried a value it cannot use: a wait of less than no time. Values: `entity`, `argument`.
- <a id="command-not-controlled"></a>`command.not_controlled`: A command that only a controller gives (`Act`, `Wait`, `Cancel`, `ClearPlan`) addressed an entity whose control is `none` (03 §5.1). Values: `entity`.
- <a id="component-missing"></a>`component.missing`: The entity has no component of the kind the change needs.
- <a id="decision-none-pending"></a>`decision.none_pending`: The entity is not waiting for a decision. Values: `entity`.
- <a id="device-no-element"></a>`device.no_element`: There is no element on that layer of the cell. Values: `layer`.
- <a id="device-none"></a>`device.none`: An element was to be promoted whose definition names no `device`. Values: `element`, the element's state as data writes it.
- <a id="device-not-registered"></a>`device.not_registered`: The definitions were loaded without the `device` definition type. Values: none.
- <a id="device-unknown-def"></a>`device.unknown_def`: The `device` an element's definition names is not a `device` definition. Values: `device`.
- <a id="engineaction-cancel-only-for"></a>`engine:action_cancel_only_for`: The actor tried to abandon an action in a phase whose `cancel` lists tags, for something that carries none of them.
  Shown as `{cap(the(self))} cannot break off for that.`.
  - `action` (id<action>): The action that was asked for.
  - `phase` (string): The id of the phase the action is in.
  - `tags` (list<string>): The tags the phase may be abandoned for.
- <a id="engineaction-cannot-cancel"></a>`engine:action_cannot_cancel`: The actor tried to abandon an action in a phase whose `cancel` is false.
  Shown as `{cap(the(self))} {verb(self, 'be')} committed.`.
  - `action` (id<action>): The action that was asked for.
  - `phase` (string): The id of the phase the action is in.
- <a id="engineaction-channel-busy"></a>`engine:action_channel_busy`: An action needs more free slots of a channel than its participant has free: other actions hold them.
  Shown as `{cap(the(self))} {verb(self, 'need')} {count($needed, $channel_name)} free and {verb(self, 'have')} {$free}.`.
  - `action` (id<action>): The action that was asked for.
  - `channel` (id<channel>): The channel concerned.
  - `channel_name` (string): What the channel is called: its `name`, or its id if it has none.
  - `needed` (int): How many free slots the action needs; for `all`, every enabled slot.
  - `free` (int): How many enabled slots are free.
  - `holders` (list<id<action>>): The actions holding the rest.
- <a id="engineaction-channel-disabled"></a>`engine:action_channel_disabled`: A channel slot an action was using was disabled: the action is interrupted.
  Shown as `{cap(the(self))} {verb(self, 'lose')} the use of {their(self)} {$channel_name}.`.
  - `action` (id<action>): The action that was asked for.
  - `channel` (id<channel>): The channel concerned.
  - `channel_name` (string): What the channel is called: its `name`, or its id if it has none.
- <a id="engineaction-channel-lacking"></a>`engine:action_channel_lacking`: An action needs more slots of a channel than its participant has enabled at all: a limb is missing, bound or broken.
  Shown as `{cap(the(self))} {verb(self, 'need')} {count($needed, $channel_name)} and {verb(self, 'have')} {$enabled}.`.
  - `action` (id<action>): The action that was asked for.
  - `channel` (id<channel>): The channel concerned.
  - `channel_name` (string): What the channel is called: its `name`, or its id if it has none.
  - `needed` (int): How many slots the action needs; for `all`, at least one.
  - `enabled` (int): How many slots of the channel the participant has that are not disabled.
- <a id="engineaction-list-length"></a>`engine:action_list_length`: A list parameter was given fewer values than its least or more than its greatest.
  Shown as `{cap($param)} takes from {$min} to {$max} and was given {$count}.`.
  - `action` (id<action>): The action that was asked for.
  - `param` (string): The parameter's name.
  - `count` (int): How many values were given.
  - `min` (int): The least the parameter takes.
  - `max` (int?): The most it takes, if it states a greatest length.
- <a id="engineaction-no-footing"></a>`engine:action_no_footing`: An action whose `footing` is true was asked of an actor with nothing under it.
  Shown as `{cap(the(self))} {verb(self, 'have')} nothing to stand on.`.
  - `action` (id<action>): The action that was asked for.
- <a id="engineaction-parameter-invalid"></a>`engine:action_parameter_invalid`: An action was asked for with a parameter whose value is null or of the wrong type.
  Shown as `That is not something {$param} can be.`.
  - `action` (id<action>): The action that was asked for.
  - `param` (string): The parameter's name.
  - `expected` (string): The type the parameter takes.
- <a id="engineaction-parameter-missing"></a>`engine:action_parameter_missing`: An action was asked for without a parameter that has no default.
  Shown as `{cap(the(self))} must say which {$param}.`.
  - `action` (id<action>): The action that was asked for.
  - `param` (string): The parameter's name.
- <a id="engineaction-requires"></a>`engine:action_requires`: An action's `requires` was false, or null, when the action was to start, or when a step of a plan came due. The action's `fail_text` is shown in place of this sentence.
  Shown as `{cap(the(self))} cannot do that now.`.
  - `action` (id<action>): The action that was asked for.
- <a id="engineaction-slot-unavailable"></a>`engine:action_slot_unavailable`: A parameter named the slot an action is to use, and that slot is held by another action, disabled, or not a slot of a channel the action uses.
  Shown as `{cap(the(self))} cannot use that for this.`.
  - `action` (id<action>): The action that was asked for.
  - `channel` (id<channel>): The channel concerned.
  - `param` (string): The parameter's name.
  - `state` (string): `held`, `disabled` or `not_a_slot`.
- <a id="engineaction-start-condition"></a>`engine:action_start_condition`: An action's `requires_at_start` was false, or null, when the action began. The action is interrupted and its `on_interrupt` runs.
  Shown as `{cap(the(self))} cannot go through with it.`.
  - `action` (id<action>): The action that was asked for.
- <a id="engineaction-transition-limit"></a>`engine:action_transition_limit`: An action changed phase without time passing more often than `rules.max_transitions` allows, and was ended with an error. A loop of phases of no length is the usual cause.
  Shown as `{cap(the(self))} {verb(self, 'lose')} the thread.`.
  - `action` (id<action>): The action that was asked for.
  - `phase` (string): The id of the phase the action is in.
  - `limit` (int): The value of `rules.max_transitions`.
- <a id="engineaction-vetoed"></a>`engine:action_vetoed`: A handler of the `ActionStarting` hook cancelled the action without naming a reason of its own.
  Shown as `Something stops {the(self)}.`.
  - `action` (id<action>): The action that was asked for.
  - `rule` (string): The id of the rule that cancelled it.
- <a id="enginereaction-cannot-cancel"></a>`engine:reaction_cannot_cancel`: A reaction needs slots held by the reactor's current actions, and one of those is in a phase that cannot be cancelled to make room.
  Shown as `{cap(the(self))} {verb(self, 'be')} committed to something else.`.
  - `action` (id<action>): The action that was asked for.
  - `channel` (id<channel>): The channel concerned.
  - `holder` (id<action>): The action holding the slot.
  - `phase` (string): The id of the phase the action is in.
- <a id="enginereaction-not-listed"></a>`engine:reaction_not_listed`: An action was offered as a reaction to a window whose kind its `reaction_to` does not list.
  Shown as `That is no answer to this.`.
  - `action` (id<action>): The action that was asked for.
  - `kind` (id<window_kind>): The kind of the window.
- <a id="enginereaction-not-on-behalf"></a>`engine:reaction_not_on_behalf`: A reaction whose `on_behalf` is false was offered to a window that does not name the reactor.
  Shown as `{cap(the(self))} cannot answer for someone else that way.`.
  - `action` (id<action>): The action that was asked for.
  - `kind` (id<window_kind>): The kind of the window.
- <a id="enginerole-declined"></a>`engine:role_declined`: A role that is not forced was offered and declined, or was not answered before the action's first phase ended.
  Shown as `{cap(the($who))} will not.`.
  - `action` (id<action>): The action that was asked for.
  - `role` (string): The role's name.
  - `who` (entity): The participant who declined.
  - `answered` (bool): False if the offer ran out unanswered.
- <a id="enginerole-participant-left"></a>`engine:role_participant_left`: A participant of a joint action was interrupted, or lost a slot the action held: the action ends for everyone in it.
  Shown as `{cap(the($who))} {verb($who, 'be')} out of it.`.
  - `action` (id<action>): The action that was asked for.
  - `role` (string): The role's name.
  - `who` (entity): The participant who was interrupted or disabled.
- <a id="enginerole-unfilled"></a>`engine:role_unfilled`: A joint action was asked for without a participant for one of its roles, or with one who no longer exists.
  Shown as `{cap(the(self))} must say who.`.
  - `action` (id<action>): The action that was asked for.
  - `role` (string): The role's name.
- <a id="enginewindow-closed"></a>`engine:window_closed`: A reaction was asked for to a window that has closed.
  Shown as `The moment has passed.`.
  - `kind` (id<window_kind>): The kind of the window.
- <a id="enginewindow-not-noticed"></a>`engine:window_not_noticed`: A window's `noticed_if` was false for the candidate, or the candidate was no candidate at all.
  Shown as `{cap(the(self))} never {verb(self, 'see')} it coming.`.
  - `kind` (id<window_kind>): The kind of the window.
- <a id="enginewindow-noticed-late"></a>`engine:window_noticed_late`: A window closed before the candidate's `notice` delay had passed on the candidate's clock.
  Shown as `{cap(the(self))} {verb(self, 'be')} too slow.`.
  - `kind` (id<window_kind>): The kind of the window.
  - `notice` (real): Seconds the candidate needed to notice.
  - `open` (real): Seconds the window stayed open.
- <a id="entity-ids-exhausted"></a>`entity.ids_exhausted`: Every entity slot has been used.
- <a id="entity-stored"></a>`entity.stored`: The entity is not in the world, so nothing can be scheduled for it. Values: `entity`.
- <a id="entity-unknown"></a>`entity.unknown`: No entity has this id: it was never created, or it has been removed. Values: `entity`.
- <a id="entity-dead"></a>`entity_dead`: The entity is dead: its mind does not drive it, so it cannot act and cannot die again. Values: `entity`.
- <a id="entity-unconscious"></a>`entity_unconscious`: The entity is unconscious: its mind does not drive it for now, so it cannot act. Values: `entity`.
- <a id="events-bad-payload"></a>`events.bad_payload`: An event was raised without a subject or field its type declares, with one it does not declare, or with one of the wrong kind. Values: `event`, `name`.
- <a id="events-cancelled"></a>`events.cancelled`: A hook was cancelled by a handler that gave no reason of its own. Values: `event`.
- <a id="events-cascade-limit"></a>`events.cascade_limit`: One pump delivered more events than `rules.max_cascade`; the rest were dropped. Values: `limit`, `dropped`, `trace`.
- <a id="events-field-fixed"></a>`events.field_fixed`: A handler tried to change a field that its hook does not declare mutable. Values: `event`, `field`.
- <a id="events-hook-depth"></a>`events.hook_depth`: A hook was raised from inside too many others and was skipped. Values: `event`, `limit`.
- <a id="events-unknown-type"></a>`events.unknown_type`: No event type has this name. Values: `event`.
- <a id="has-mind"></a>`has_mind`: The entity already has a mind: `create_mind` in it, or `transfer_mind` into it without `swap`. Values: `entity`.
- <a id="interaction-bad-argument"></a>`interaction.bad_argument`: A verb of interactions was given an argument that is missing or of the wrong kind. Values: `verb`, `arg`.
- <a id="interaction-no-target"></a>`interaction.no_target`: The target no longer exists, or its cell is not loaded. Values: `interaction`.
- <a id="interaction-not-now"></a>`interaction.not_now`: The interaction's `if` does not hold; the message is its `fail_text`. Values: `interaction`.
- <a id="interaction-not-offered"></a>`interaction.not_offered`: The target does not offer the interaction: its definition does not list it, it is not `offered_by: any`, or it is done to the other kind of target. Values: `interaction`.
- <a id="interaction-not-registered"></a>`interaction.not_registered`: The definitions were loaded without the `interaction` definition type. Values: none.
- <a id="interaction-out-of-reach"></a>`interaction.out_of_reach`: The user cannot reach the target by the interaction's `reach`, and no handler of `interaction_reach` let it. Values: `interaction`, `reach`.
- <a id="interaction-unknown"></a>`interaction.unknown`: The id is not an `interaction` definition. Values: `interaction`.
- <a id="item-bad-amount"></a>`item.bad_amount`: A share to repair, or a packet's energy or intensity, is negative or not finite. Values: `amount`.
- <a id="item-bad-argument"></a>`item.bad_argument`: A verb of items was given an argument that is missing or of the wrong kind. Values: `arg`, the argument's name.
- <a id="item-bad-count"></a>`item.bad_count`: A count is zero, or is not less than the stack holds where some must stay. Values: `count`, `have`.
- <a id="item-does-not-fit"></a>`item.does_not_fit`: The thing takes more volume or weighs more than the container has room for. Values: `item`, `container`, `what` (`volume` or `mass`), `needed`, `room`.
- <a id="item-layer-taken"></a>`item.layer_taken`: A part the item would cover already wears something at that layer. Values: `item`, `part`, `layer`, `by`.
- <a id="item-no-body"></a>`item.no_body`: Something with no body was to hold a thing in a grasp or wear it. Values: `entity`.
- <a id="item-no-container"></a>`item.no_container`: Nothing the holder wears or holds would take the thing. Values: `who`, `item`.
- <a id="item-no-free-grasp"></a>`item.no_free_grasp`: The holder's working parts supply fewer free slots of a channel than the thing's `grip` needs. Values: `holder`, `channel`, `needed`, `free`.
- <a id="item-no-grip"></a>`item.no_grip`: The thing has no `grip`, so it cannot be held in a grasp. Values: `item`.
- <a id="item-no-part-to-wear-on"></a>`item.no_part_to_wear_on`: The wearer's body has no outer part that the item's `wear` selects. Values: `item`, `wearer`.
- <a id="item-not-a-container"></a>`item.not_a_container`: Something was to be put into a thing whose definition has no `holds`. Values: `container`.
- <a id="item-not-accepted"></a>`item.not_accepted`: The container's `accepts` lists none of the thing's tags. Values: `item`, `container`.
- <a id="item-not-an-item"></a>`item.not_an_item`: The entity has no `Item` component. Values: `entity`.
- <a id="item-not-contained"></a>`item.not_contained`: A thing that is not stowed in or enclosed by anything was to be taken out. Values: `item`.
- <a id="item-not-equal"></a>`item.not_equal`: Two items were to be merged that are not equal in every respect, or are not in the same hold. Values: `item`, `into`.
- <a id="item-not-held"></a>`item.not_held`: The thing is inside nothing, so it cannot be dropped or given. Values: `item`.
- <a id="item-not-registered"></a>`item.not_registered`: The definitions were loaded without the `item` definition type. Values: none.
- <a id="item-not-stackable"></a>`item.not_stackable`: More than one was asked of a definition that does not `stack`. Values: `item`.
- <a id="item-not-wearable"></a>`item.not_wearable`: The item has no `wear`. Values: `item`.
- <a id="item-not-worn"></a>`item.not_worn`: An item that is not worn was to be taken off. Values: `item`.
- <a id="item-unknown-def"></a>`item.unknown_def`: An item was to be made from an id that is not an `item` definition. Values: `def`.
- <a id="move-bad-argument"></a>`move.bad_argument`: A movement verb was given something it does not take: a `who` that is not an entity, a `to` that is not a cell. Carries `argument`.
- <a id="move-bad-direction"></a>`move.bad_direction`: A direction was not one of `north`, `north_east`, `east`, `south_east`, `south`, `south_west`, `west`, `north_west`, `up` and `down`. Carries `dir`.
- <a id="move-blocked"></a>`move.blocked`: Something stands in the cell that the mover cannot step over and that has no state in which it stands aside: a wall. Carries `height`, in metres.
- <a id="move-cannot-move"></a>`move.cannot_move`: The mover has no way of moving that works now: it lists none and no definition is its default, its posture allows none, its body lacks the channel slots, or every `speed` comes to nothing. Also given for a step that none of its ways of moving makes, where nothing more particular applies. Carries `entity`.
- <a id="move-closed"></a>`move.closed`: What stands in the cell could stand aside and does not: a closed door. Carries `height`.
- <a id="move-corner"></a>`move.corner`: A diagonal step would pass a cell with something in the way: movers do not cut corners.
- <a id="move-edge"></a>`move.edge`: There is no cell to step into: it is not loaded, or lies beyond an edge of the realm. Carries `dir`.
- <a id="move-goal-blocked"></a>`move.goal_blocked`: The mover believes it cannot be in the goal cell at all.
- <a id="move-in-flight"></a>`move.in_flight`: The world is carrying the mover as a body (02 §15): it is falling or thrown, and steps and placements wait until it lands. Carries `entity`.
- <a id="move-liquid"></a>`move.liquid`: The cell is liquid and the mover has no way of moving through liquid.
- <a id="move-no-footing"></a>`move.no_footing`: There is nothing to stand on in the cell and the mover cannot be there otherwise. A step given `drop` is made all the same, and the mover falls.
- <a id="move-no-path"></a>`move.no_path`: `follow_path` was called for a mover that is following no path, or has reached the end of it.
- <a id="move-no-room"></a>`move.no_room`: A mover wider or taller than a cell does not fit where the step would put it.
- <a id="move-no-way"></a>`move.no_way`: No path leads to the goal: every cell the mover believes it can reach was tried, or the search settled as many cells as it may (`searched`) without reaching it.
- <a id="move-nowhere"></a>`move.nowhere`: The mover is not standing in the world: it is inside something or stored. Carries `entity`.
- <a id="move-occupied"></a>`move.occupied`: Another occupant that blocks movement fills the cell on a plane the mover shares, and did not yield. Carries `by`, the occupant.
- <a id="move-off-path"></a>`move.off_path`: The mover is not where its path left it, or an earlier step of the path was refused: the path must be planned again.
- <a id="move-other-grid"></a>`move.other_grid`: The goal is in another grid than the mover.
- <a id="move-too-far"></a>`move.too_far`: No path was found within the cost allowed. Carries `max_cost`, in metres of travel.
- <a id="move-too-steep"></a>`move.too_steep`: There is no way up or down here for this mover: no ramp, stairs or ladder it can take, or a floor between.
- <a id="move-unknown-movement"></a>`move.unknown_movement`: A way of moving was named that no loaded definition has.
- <a id="no-free-socket"></a>`no_free_socket`: The socket is full, or no socket of the part would take the new one. Values: `entity`, `part`.
- <a id="no-mind"></a>`no_mind`: The entity has no mind: there is none to move, remove, stop or start, and nothing to act for it unless it has a driver. Values: `entity`.
- <a id="no-such-layer"></a>`no_such_layer`: The part has no layer of that number; the outermost is 0. Values: `entity`, `part`, `layer`.
- <a id="no-such-socket"></a>`no_such_socket`: The part a new part is to go on has no socket of that name. Values: `entity`, `part`, `socket`.
- <a id="no-templates"></a>`no_templates`: A spec names no template.
- <a id="not-a-part"></a>`not_a_part`: What was to be grafted is not a part that came off a body. Values: `item`, when an item was given.
- <a id="not-dead"></a>`not_dead`: `revive` of an entity that is not dead. Values: `entity`.
- <a id="part-name-taken"></a>`part_name_taken`: A part that is there already has the name. Values: `entity`, `name`.
- <a id="perception-bad-value"></a>`perception.bad_value`: A strength, level, confidence, salience, facing or bonus out of its range, or an argument that names nothing. Values: `value` or `argument`.
- <a id="perception-field-not-sent"></a>`perception.field_not_sent`: A signal of the `field` model is read from a field where the observer stands and cannot be given off. Values: `kind`.
- <a id="perception-has-sense"></a>`perception.has_sense`: The entity has that sense already. Values: `entity`, `sense`.
- <a id="perception-no-sense"></a>`perception.no_sense`: The entity does not have that sense. Values: `entity`, `sense`.
- <a id="perception-no-senses"></a>`perception.no_senses`: The entity has no senses: it cannot face or search. Values: `entity`.
- <a id="perception-self-track"></a>`perception.self_track`: A mind keeps no track of itself. Values: `entity`.
- <a id="perception-unknown-kind"></a>`perception.unknown_kind`: The signal kind named is not one of the loaded definitions'. Values: `kind`.
- <a id="perception-unknown-sense"></a>`perception.unknown_sense`: The sense named is not one of the loaded definitions'. Values: `sense`.
- <a id="physical-bad-measure"></a>`physical.bad_measure`: A mass, volume, height or cross-section is negative or not finite.
- <a id="posture-unknown"></a>`posture.unknown`: A posture was named that no loaded definition has.
- <a id="relocate-inside-itself"></a>`relocate.inside_itself`: An entity cannot be put inside itself or inside something it contains. Values: `entity`, `container`.
- <a id="relocate-too-deep"></a>`relocate.too_deep`: Things are nested more deeply than the engine allows. Values: `entity`, `limit`.
- <a id="replay-diverged"></a>`replay.diverged`: A replayed input log no longer matches the simulation: an entry could not be reached or was refused. Values: `entry`.
- <a id="rule-bad-argument"></a>`rule.bad_argument`: A rule was called with a parameter it does not have, without one that has no default, or with a value of the wrong type. The call was refused and gave null. Values: `rule`, `path`, `parameter`.
- <a id="rule-bad-key"></a>`rule.bad_key`: A key of a place does not fit what is there: a key of something that is neither a map nor a list, an index outside a list, a key that is not a text or an id. Nothing was written. Values: `rule`, `path`.
- <a id="rule-call-depth"></a>`rule.call_depth`: Rules called each other more deeply than `rules.max_call_depth`. The call was refused and gave null; the caller carried on. Values: `rule`, `path`, `limit`.
- <a id="rule-choice-lost"></a>`rule.choice_lost`: A choice put by `ask` was answered, and the `ask` is no longer where it was written when the choice was put: the definitions changed under a save. The option's effects did not run. Values: `definition`, `path`.
- <a id="rule-choice-refused"></a>`rule.choice_refused`: The `Choose` command named an option the choice does not have, or one whose `if` did not hold when the choice was put. The choice is still waiting. Values: `choice`, `option`.
- <a id="rule-emit-refused"></a>`rule.emit_refused`: The simulation refused to raise an event: it is one of the engine's own, or what was given does not match its type. Values: `rule`, `path`, `reason`.
- <a id="rule-expression-warning"></a>`rule.expression_warning`: An expression that a rule or a list of effects evaluated gave a run-time warning (05 §4.5): a division by zero, a value of the wrong type. The operation gave null and the rule carried on. Values: `definition`, `path`, `count`.
- <a id="rule-message-refused"></a>`rule.message_refused`: A `message` was for something that is not an entity, or the simulation would not deliver it. Nothing was shown. Values: `rule`, `path`.
- <a id="rule-no-random"></a>`rule.no_random`: `weighted` had to choose at random and the simulation has no stream to draw from. No entry was run. Values: `rule`, `path`.
- <a id="rule-no-subject"></a>`rule.no_subject`: An effect needed a subject (whose variable to set, what to attach a rule to) and was given null or a value that is not a subject. The effect was skipped. Values: `rule`, `path`.
- <a id="rule-not-a-hook"></a>`rule.not_a_hook`: `modify` or `cancel_event` ran where the event being handled is not a hook. Nothing was changed. Values: `rule`, `path`.
- <a id="rule-not-attachable"></a>`rule.not_attachable`: `attach_rule` was given a rule that is not an attached rule: one that listens for no event, or one that runs for every event of its type. Nothing was attached. Values: `rule`, `path`.
- <a id="rule-queries-unavailable"></a>`rule.queries_unavailable`: `for_each` was given a query that did not compile: the body did not run. Values: `rule`, `path`.
- <a id="rule-queue-limit"></a>`rule.queue_limit`: More rules were queued than `rules.max_queued` before the queue was emptied. The rule was not queued. Values: `rule`, `path`, `limit`.
- <a id="rule-step-limit"></a>`rule.step_limit`: A run executed more effects and loop iterations than `rules.max_steps`, counting those of the rules it called. The run was ended; what it had done stays done. Values: `rule`, `path`, `limit`.
- <a id="rule-timer-lost"></a>`rule.timer_lost`: A timer fell due, and the `after` or `every` that set it, or the recurring rule it runs, is no longer among the definitions: they changed under a save (05 §13.4). Nothing ran and the timer was dropped. Values: `definition`, `path` or `rule`.
- <a id="rule-timer-refused"></a>`rule.timer_refused`: `after` or `every` could not set its timer (05 §10.4): its time came to null or to no time at all, `times` was not an int, or its owner is nothing on a clock (an entity, a cell, an area, a site, a realm or the simulation). Nothing was scheduled and the rule carried on. Values: `rule`, `path`, and `reason` for one the simulation gave.
- <a id="rule-timers-unavailable"></a>`rule.timers_unavailable`: `after` or `every` ran against a host that keeps no timers (the rule runtime's test host). Nothing was scheduled. Values: `rule`, `path`.
- <a id="rule-type-mismatch"></a>`rule.type_mismatch`: A value had a type the effect does not accept, where the type was not known at load: `add` to something that is neither a number nor a list, a `repeat` count that is not an int, a weight that is not a number, a list to iterate that is not a list, a returned value that is not of the rule's `returns`. The effect was skipped. Values: `rule`, `path`.
- <a id="rule-unknown-rule"></a>`rule.unknown_rule`: An expression that should give the id of a rule gave something else, or the id of a rule that did not load. The call was refused. Values: `rule`, `path`.
- <a id="rule-value-too-deep"></a>`rule.value_too_deep`: An effect would have written a value whose lists and maps nest more deeply than `rules.max_value_depth`. Nothing was written. Values: `rule`, `path`, `limit`.
- <a id="rule-value-too-large"></a>`rule.value_too_large`: An effect would have written a list or a map of more elements, or a text of more bytes, than `rules.max_value_size`. Nothing was written. Values: `rule`, `path`, `limit`.
- <a id="rule-verb-refused"></a>`rule.verb_refused`: A verb declined. The effect did nothing and the rule carried on. Values: `rule`, `path`, `verb`, `reason` (the code of the verb's reason).
- <a id="rule-verb-unbound"></a>`rule.verb_unbound`: An effect called a verb that is in the registry and that nothing in the engine carries out: a verb of a package that is not built into this simulation. Nothing was done. Values: `verb`.
- <a id="rule-write-refused"></a>`rule.write_refused`: The simulation refused to set or remove a variable or a property. Values: `rule`, `path`, `reason` (the code of the simulation's reason).
- <a id="same-entity"></a>`same_entity`: An entity was named as its own driver, or as where its own mind is to go. Values: `entity`.
- <a id="socket-refuses"></a>`socket_refuses`: The socket does not take that kind of part: its `accepts` does not list it. Values: `entity`, `part`, `socket`.
- <a id="stats-expression-warning"></a>`stats.expression_warning`: A fault, not a refusal: an expression of an attribute or a pool raised a run-time warning while it was worked out. Values: `entity`, `count`, `warning`.
- <a id="subject-gone"></a>`subject.gone`: What was to be written to no longer exists, or the place's subject came to something that is not a subject. Values: `kind`.
- <a id="templates-not-registered"></a>`templates_not_registered`: The definitions were loaded without the `template` definition type.
- <a id="time-refused"></a>`time.refused`: The timeline refused; the message says why.
- <a id="too-many-parts"></a>`too_many_parts`: The body would have more than 1024 parts. Values: none.
- <a id="trait-bad-argument"></a>`trait.bad_argument`: A verb of traits was given an argument that is missing or of the wrong kind. Values: `arg`, the argument's name.
- <a id="trait-bad-duration"></a>`trait.bad_duration`: A duration given to `add_trait`, or left by a handler of `trait_adding`, is not a finite time above zero. Values: `duration`, in seconds.
- <a id="trait-bad-stacks"></a>`trait.bad_stacks`: A count of stacks to remove is not a whole number above zero. Values: `stacks`.
- <a id="trait-not-registered"></a>`trait.not_registered`: The definitions were loaded without the `trait` definition type. Values: none.
- <a id="trait-unknown"></a>`trait.unknown`: The id is not a `trait` definition. Values: `trait`, as given.
- <a id="unknown-choice"></a>`unknown_choice`: A selection names a choice none of the spec's templates has. Values: `choice`.
- <a id="unknown-material"></a>`unknown_material`: The id is not a material. Values: none.
- <a id="unknown-part"></a>`unknown_part`: The id is not a `body_part` definition. Values: none.
- <a id="unknown-template"></a>`unknown_template`: An id names no template. Values: `what`.
- <a id="vars-too-deep"></a>`vars.too_deep`: A value's lists and maps are nested more deeply than a variable may hold. Values: `variable`, `limit`.
- <a id="vars-wrong-scope"></a>`vars.wrong_scope`: A declared variable was set on a subject of another kind than it was declared for, or a variable was set on an element. Values: `variable`, `declared`, `found`.
- <a id="vars-wrong-type"></a>`vars.wrong_type`: A declared variable was given a value that is not of its declared type. Values: `variable`, `declared`, `found`.
- <a id="verb-bad-argument"></a>`verb.bad_argument`: A verb was given an argument it cannot use: null where a value is needed, a subject of another kind than the verb takes, or a word that is not one of those it knows. Nothing was done. Values: `verb`, `argument`.
- <a id="window-unknown-kind"></a>`window.unknown_kind`: A window was to be opened with a kind that is not loaded, or every number a window can have has been given out. Values: `kind`.
- <a id="world-bad-argument"></a>`world.bad_argument`: A world verb was given an argument that is missing or of the wrong kind. Values: `verb`, `arg`.
- <a id="world-no-element"></a>`world.no_element`: The cell has no element on the layer the verb acts on. Values: `layer`.
- <a id="world-not-in-world"></a>`world.not_in_world`: An entity to be thrown is not standing in the world, or one to be pushed or caught is not in flight. Values: `entity`.
- <a id="world-not-loaded"></a>`world.not_loaded`: The cell's tract is not loaded.
- <a id="world-outside-realm"></a>`world.outside_realm`: The cell lies beyond an edge of its realm.
- <a id="world-refused"></a>`world.refused`: The world refused the change; the message says why.
- <a id="world-tract-failed"></a>`world.tract_failed`: A tract could not be loaded or unloaded at a safe point; the message says why. It is tried again when something changes. Values: `realm`, `x`, `y`.
- <a id="world-unknown-area"></a>`world.unknown_area`: No area has this id.
- <a id="world-unknown-def"></a>`world.unknown_def`: An id names no damage type, material, field or area kind the world has. Values: `def`.
- <a id="world-unknown-grid"></a>`world.unknown_grid`: No grid has this id.
- <a id="world-unknown-realm"></a>`world.unknown_realm`: No realm has this id.
- <a id="world-unknown-state"></a>`world.unknown_state`: A state as written (`def`, `def@material`, `def#state`) names no definition of the layer, no material or no state of the definition. Values: `state`.
- <a id="write-bad-key"></a>`write.bad_key`: A key of a place names no element of the list, is not a text or an id for a map, or steps into what has no entries. Values: `length` for a list.
- <a id="write-bad-value"></a>`write.bad_value`: A settable property was given a value it cannot take; the message says what it takes. Values: `found`, `property`.
- <a id="write-cannot-add"></a>`write.cannot_add`: `add` was given what cannot be added to what is there: it adds to numbers and appends to lists.
- <a id="write-not-a-subject"></a>`write.not_a_subject`: The place is a local or a field of the event, which whoever runs the rule keeps and assigns.
- <a id="write-not-settable"></a>`write.not_settable`: The subject has no such property, or the property cannot be set. Values: `kind`, `property`.

## The console's host

- `console.decision_pending`: Time cannot pass: a rule has put a choice to a directly controlled entity and nobody is there to answer it. An entity that is only free to act waits instead. Values: `entity`.
- `console.no_active`: `@self` was asked for and no character is active. `control <who> direct` makes one active.
- `console.no_cursor`: `@here` was asked for and there is no cursor. `gen` and `look` put it somewhere.
- `console.no_game`: No simulation is running. `use <profile>` starts one.
- `console.no_world`: The simulation has no realm. `gen <kind>` makes one.
- `console.not_a_place`: An argument that should be a cell, or something that is in one, is not.
- `console.not_an_entity`: An argument that should be an entity is not.
- `console.not_built`: The command is registered and nothing carries it out yet. Values: `command`.
- `console.nothing_selected`: `@sel` was asked for and nothing is selected.
- `console.rules_unbound`: A verb, a rule or an effect was asked for of a host whose rule runtime is not bound to its simulation. The host over the real simulation carries them out and no longer gives this. Values: `command`.
- `console.too_large`: `gen` was asked for a world of more tracts a side than it builds. Values: `size`, `max`.
- `console.unknown_kind`: A word that should name a kind of world, a kind of occupant, a damage type, a field or an element state names none. Values: `what`, `name`.
- `console.unknown_name`: A reference `@name` to a name that no command gave with `as=`. Values: `name`.
- `console.unknown_reference`: A reference `@kind:name` of a kind the host does not have, or to something that is not there. Values: `kind`, `name`.
- `console.unknown_subsystem`: `hash` was asked for a subsystem it does not know. Values: `subsystem`.
